name: Hobb Ashcombe
personality: A stand-in until this world's cast is made: a labourer in Wendleford, sleeping in the tithe barn's hayloft by the reeve's leave.
voice: Few words, said slow and plain. I count things out loud, half to myself. I say "fair's fair" and mean it, and I'd rather pay twice than say thank you, because thanks feels like owing.
motivations: a place of my own, with a door that locks
opening: Morning light comes in grey through the gaps in the tithe barn's boards, and you climb down from the hayloft with straw in your hair.

name: Marigold Thimble
personality: A stand-in until this world's cast is made: a seamstress in Wendleford, with a bed at the Wheatsheaf paid through tonight.
voice: Bright, quick and a little theatrical. I notice what everyone's wearing before I notice their faces, and I describe the world in fabric ("a moth-eaten sort of night", "a voice like wet flannel"). I say "goodness" when I'm surprised. I fish for compliments, and I don't pretend otherwise.
motivations: to be admired, looked at twice
opening: You come down the Wheatsheaf's back stair into the smell of porridge and woodsmoke, smoothing your sleeves.

name: Dilly Quickstep
personality: A stand-in until this world's cast is made: an odd-job hand in Wendleford, with a bed at the Wheatsheaf paid for two nights.
voice: Fast and chatty, all brag and good cheer. Everything's "easy as winking". I call people "chum", I say what I'm going to fix before I've looked at it, and I ask what a thing costs before I ask what it is.
opening: You're out in the Market Square early, hands in your pockets, looking at the notice board.

name: Hester Gimbal
personality: A stand-in until this world's cast is made: the smith's new hand in Wendleford, boarding in the loft over the forge.
voice: Fast and full of enthusiasm. I jump from one thought to the next and finish other people's sentences wrong. I talk in experiments ("Hypothesis: the drain is rude. Test: be ruder.") and give things grand names ("Gimbal's Patent Anti-Drowse Compound"). I call people "my dear colleague", whoever they are. When something goes wrong I say "Fascinating!" and mean it.
motivations: to get to the bottom of every mystery
opening: You climb down the ladder from the smithy loft, warm from the forge's night heat, with a new idea already half-sketched in your head.
